name: Edison Electric Institute

summary.text: The Edison Electric Institute (EEI) is the trade association that, by its own description in regulatory testimony, represents all U.S. investor-owned electric companies. Presidential science adviser Donald Hornig told EEI's 1968 annual convention that carbon dioxide from fossil fuels could affect the climate, and MIT professor Carroll Wilson gave a similar warning at its 1971 convention. In 1991 EEI, the National Coal Association and the Western Fuels Association funded the Information Council on the Environment, an advertising campaign whose stated goal was to 'reposition global warming as theory (not fact)'. A 2022 peer-reviewed study in Environmental Research Letters, reviewing 188 industry documents from 1968 to 2019, found that EEI and the Electric Power Research Institute authored or distributed most of the documents and that the industry moved from denial in the 1980s and 1990s to a strategy of delay after acknowledging the scientific consensus in the 2000s.

facts.claim: In testimony filed with the Missouri Public Service Commission, EEI described itself as representing all U.S. investor-owned electric companies and providing services, resources, expertise and networks on issues affecting the energy industry. Utilities have sought to recover EEI dues from customers in rate cases.
facts.quote: provide services, resources, expertise and established networks on all issues that impact the energy industry.

sources.title: Testimony describing the Edison Electric Institute

facts.claim: Donald F. Hornig, science adviser to President Lyndon Johnson, addressed EEI's 1968 annual convention on carbon dioxide and its possible climate effects, telling utility executives that carbon dioxide is the chief heat-absorbing component of the atmosphere. The speech was documented in the 2017 'Utilities Knew' report by the Energy and Policy Institute.
facts.quote: "Carbon dioxide is not toxic, but it is the chief heat-absorbing component of the atmosphere," Donald F. Hornig said at the 1968 annual convention of the Edison Electric Institute.

facts.claim: On 9 June 1971, MIT management professor Carroll Wilson warned utility executives about carbon dioxide and climate at EEI's annual convention.
facts.quote: Carroll Wilson, an MIT management professor, spoke at EEI's 1971 annual convention. It was June 9, 1971.

facts.claim: A 1989 EEI article stated that any plan calling for urgent and extreme action to reduce utility CO2 emissions was 'premature at best', according to a 2022 study in Environmental Research Letters.
facts.quote: A 1989 Edison Electric Institute article stated that "any plan calling for urgent and extreme action to reduce utility CO2 emissions is premature at best."

facts.claim: The Information Council on the Environment (ICE), formed in 1991 and funded by the Edison Electric Institute, the National Coal Association and the Western Fuels Association, ran $510,000 of test advertising campaigns from February to August 1991. Its strategy documents stated the goal to 'reposition global warming as theory (not fact)', and an EEI letter about the Flagstaff test said the sponsor wanted to see 'how the science approach sells'.
facts.quote: Its goal was summarized as "reposition global warming as theory (not fact)," and the group was funded by the Edison Electrical Institute, the National Coal Association, and the Western Fuels Association.

facts.claim: A 2022 study in Environmental Research Letters by Emily Williams, S.A. Bartone, E.K. Swanson and Leah Stokes reviewed 188 documents from utilities, trade associations and front groups dated 1968 to 2019. It found that EEI and the Electric Power Research Institute authored or distributed most of the documents, that the industry joined oil and gas companies in casting doubt on climate science in the 1980s and co-founded front groups in the 1990s, and that after publicly acknowledging the consensus in the 2000s it shifted to a strategy of delay.
facts.quote: The Edison Electric Institute and the Electric Power Research Institute authored or distributed most of the documents in the study, and are the utility industry's main trade group and research arm, respectively.

facts.claim: State regulators have differed on whether utility customers may be charged for EEI dues. The California Public Utilities Commission disallowed recovery of $1.552 million in EEI dues in a Southern California Edison rate case, finding the utility had not shown any portion was recoverable from ratepayers; the Michigan Public Service Commission allowed DTE Energy to recover its EEI dues from customers.
facts.quote: the CPUC later disallowed the EEI dues, finding the utility had not shown that any portion was recoverable from ratepayers.

connections.claim: Southern Company's chief executive Thomas Fanning served as chairman of the Edison Electric Institute, according to Southern Company's own announcement of an EEI leadership award.
connections.quote: He is also a past chairman of the Conference of Chairs of the Federal Reserve Banks and the Edison Electric Institute (EEI).

openQuestions: Whether EEI itself is or was a member of ALEC was not established; the sources found concern individual utilities' ALEC dues.
The year of Fanning's EEI chairmanship was not established from the sources found.
The 2022 Environmental Research Letters paper was cited from its journal page and a university release; the full text should be checked for the exact 1989 EEI article citation.
The 1971 Carroll Wilson address is documented in the Energy and Policy Institute report; the site's page attributes a 1971 warning to Donald Hornig, whose address was in 1968.
